To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Dropout, when applied to a one-hidden-layer neural network, can be shown to decrease (up to a certain approximation) the training objective function by a multiplicative constant.

(i) dropout is a “stabilizing” regularizer for convex empirical risk minimization; (ii) it provides fast generalization error rates for convex generalized linear models; (iii) dropout can be used to design differentially private algorithms; and (iv) dropout significantly outperformed the L2-regularization based methods on several benchmark datasets.
1. Dropout, a widely used heuristics in training DBNs, can be rigorously justified as a technique that can avoid local minima (upto an error term) when training a one-hidden layer NN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.

the question of “to drop or not to drop?” We provide theoretical guarantees that dropout indeed helps avoid poor local minima for training DBNs, while also showing that it acts as a regularizer for convex ERM problems.

the following questions: (1) Can we provide theoretical justification for the empirical successes of dropout? (2) What is the effect of dropout on the training objective function? and (3) How can we exploit the stability of dropout for designing efficient algorithms for learning and privacy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dropout technique is not only a simple heuristic, but also provides theoretical guarantees for training deep belief networks, convex ERMs and GLMs.
dropout is a very useful tool for training deep belief networks, but is not as effective for training convex ERMs.
the dropout technique is a powerful and robust tool for training DBNs, and also for learning convex GLMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dropout technique, which is widely used in practice, can be justified theoretically.
dropout is a robust, consistent and stable method for learning convex and non-convex functions.
we rigorously establish the stability and consistency properties of the widely used dropout technique.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dropout technique can be used to obtain provably robust and consistent algorithms for training deep networks.
dropout can be used to design robust, stable and differentially private algorithms in the context of learning convex ERM.
dropout is in fact a very useful and powerful heuristic, and its use should be encouraged in training deep belief networks.
